To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the free-living amoeba is a common cause of keratitis in contact lenses.
contact lenses are a potential source of free-living pathogenic amoebae.
the free-living amoeba Vermamoeba is the causative agent for keratitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of free-living amebae from contact lenses.
the isolation of free-living Acanthamoebae from contact lens cases and paraphernalia of Iranian patients with keratitis.
the isolation of pathogenic FLA from contact lenses of patients suffering from keratitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soft contact lens wearers should be aware of the potential risk of keratitis and should be educated to avoid the risk.
FLA keratitis is a serious disease and the use of soft contact lenses is a major risk factor.
the soft contact lens wearers with unilateral keratitis should be evaluated for the presence of Vermamonas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
contact lenses and their accessories should be disinfected properly and replaced in time to prevent the occurrence of keratitis.
contact lenses of patients suffering from keratitis should be tested for the presence and type of FLA.
the soft contact lens wearers should avoid using soft contact lenses for more than 12 h per day and should not sleep with them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of soft contact lenses should be avoided in patients suffering from keratitis.
the soft contact lenses should be used properly, as well as the lenses should be disinfected and cleaned according to the manufacturer instructions.
the contact lenses of keratitis patients should always be examined for pathogenic free living amoebae.
